records.cpicRecommendationVerbatim: Avoid clopidogrel if possible. Use prasugrel or ticagrelor at standard dose if no contraindication.

cpicImplicationsVerbatim.CYP2C19: Significantly reduced clopidogrel active metabolite formation; increased on-treatment platelet reactivity; increased risk for adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events

records.cpicCommentsVerbatim: For cardiovascular indications of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and/or percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). ACS and/or PCI includes patients undergoing PCI for an ACS or non-ACS (elective) indication.
records.patientText: Your CYP2C19 result may mean clopidogrel works less well for this condition. Discuss the result with your prescriber or pharmacist.
records.clinicianSummary: CPIC guidance for CYP2C19 poor metabolizers with ACS or PCI supports considering an alternative antiplatelet when appropriate. Review the full guideline and contraindications.

records.cpicRecommendationVerbatim: If considering clopidogrel, use at standard dose (75 mg/day)

cpicImplicationsVerbatim.CYP2C19: Normal clopidogrel active metabolite formation; normal on-treatment platelet reactivity

records.cpicCommentsVerbatim: For cardiovascular indications of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and/or percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). ACS and/or PCI includes patients undergoing PCI for an ACS or non-ACS (elective) indication.
records.patientText: This guideline does not link this CYP2C19 result to a difference in how clopidogrel works. Other factors still affect treatment.
records.clinicianSummary: The CPIC guideline does not call for a CYP2C19-based change for a normal metabolizer with ACS or PCI. Review the full guideline and patient context.
